# Worker migration contracts

These fixtures were frozen from the original JavaScript Worker on 2026-10-03, before the production migration. `routes.json` contains the 65 real Hono method/path registrations; `schema.json` contains the 12 initialized D1 tables and their indexes; the other JSON files contain public-config fields and stable deployment declarations. No credentials, cloud resource IDs or production data are copied here. A `.js` → `.ts` entry extension change is allowed by the configuration comparison.

Run `pnpm test:worker` after the Worker build. `scripts/run-worker-contracts.mjs` passes the exact `.wrangler/ts-build/index.js` artifact to fresh ephemeral Miniflare instances. `node scripts/run-worker-contracts.mjs --baseline` replays the ignored original `.wrangler/migration-baseline/index.js`. Frozen fixtures must not be regenerated to make a failing migration pass. `capture-contract-baseline.mjs --freeze-original-js` refuses both migrated entry points and existing fixtures.

The harness ignores Wrangler account/resource credentials. D1 init only runs against its own local emulator. All fetch egress is intercepted by explicit fixtures; unexpected requests and swallowed fixture assertion failures are reported during teardown. Provider fixtures capture the actual SDK request DTO. Native Email.send uses Miniflare's real email emulator, sender/destination restrictions and generated binary attachment files, rather than a success stub.

Coverage includes API/assets/object dispatch, CORS, raw Authorization/JWT/KV, public-token mode, password login, permission errors, list projections/cursors, OAuth identity/setup/binding/replay, PostalMime/CID/plus addressing, R2/KV metadata/keys/shared references, native sending, Resend reply/mixed/error/status callback, notification retries, optional AI/failure narrowing, hourly/half-hour scheduled branches, cleanup exclusions, and fresh/repeat/historical init.

`mail-storage-edge.test.mjs` adds original-bundle-verified cases for repeated CID first-match behavior, independent D1 references sharing a content-hash object key, R2 OSS GET/HEAD bytes and response metadata, native sending of reloaded R2 body images, and attachment persistence failure after object writes. Its controlled many-chunk stream invokes the actual compiled inbound callback with real local D1/KV/R2; this checks the callback's stream consumption, rather than claiming the emulator preserves arbitrary SMTP transport chunk boundaries. It uses ASCII MIME/base64 chunks and does not change the known raw UTF-8/binary decoding behavior.

Emulator limits: Miniflare 4.20260507.1 exposes email triggers through experimental `unsafeTriggerHandlers`; a rejected email may still give trigger HTTP 200. Tests verify no persistence and separately call the actual compiled production handler with a recording `setReject` callback. Scheduled UTC-midnight checks use actual wall time and are not forced by `scheduledTime`; full boundary-time verification and real SMTP/provider delivery remain outside this suite.

Known unsafe JS behavior is diagnosed rather than enshrined as a desired contract: a provider can accept before D1 insertion fails, and scheduled recovery may leave `is_del=1`. Later dedicated fixes may change these observations without changing the healthy API contract assertions.
